radiology_notes.text:
CONTRAST-ENHANCED CT OF LIVER AND UPPER ABDOMEN

INDICATION:  ___ male with known cirrhosis and abnormalities in
segment II and segment VI of the right lobe of liver.

COMPARISON:  Reference is made to a recent contrast-enhanced MR of abdomen
dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT-acquired axial images were obtained from the lung
bases to the level of the renal hila after administration of intravenous
contrast.  Arterial and portal venous phase sequences were obtained.  The
procedure was performed immediately following percutaneous radiofrequency
ablation of the segment V/VI lesion.

CT OF UPPER ABDOMEN:
There are tiny bilateral pleural effusions with adjacent compressive
atelectasis.  No pneumothorax noted. 
There is bilateral gynecomastia.  
The liver has a coarse irregular surface in keeping with known cirrhosis.  The
spleen is enlarged measuring 14.5 cm in long axis.  There are periesophageal
and splenic hilar varices. Note is made of a recanalized umbilical
vein.Findings are in keeping with portal hypertension.
In the left lobe there is a 16 x 15 x 7 mm arterial enhancing segment II
exophytic lesion. The lesion is closely related to the lesser curve of stomach
and transverse colon.  Findings are stable since the recent MR of abdomen.
Satisfactory appearance of the ablated lesion in segment VI of the right
hepatic lobe.  There is  satisfactory ___ enhancement around the
segment V / VI lesion with a 2.3 x 4.6 x 3.4 cm low attenuation ablation zone.
The common duct is normal in caliber measuring 8 mm at the level of the
ampulla.  No intrahepatic biliary dilatation.  There is a small volume of
perihepatic free fluid, most notably around the dome of liver.  The portal
veins are patent.     Post procedural changes along the percutaneous access
tract are noted in the right flank.  
No other arterial enhancing lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:  
1. Satisfactory appearance post-RF ablation of the previously noted 23 x 28 cm
enhancing lesion spanning segment V and VI of the right hepatic lobe. 
2. Stable appearance of the exophytic segment II lesion, which was not
amenable to RF ablation.
3. Changes of cirrhosis as described.


OSSEOUS STRUCTURE:  Mild degenerative changes are seen involving the lower
thoracic spine with anterior osteophyte formation:  No lytic or sclerotic bone
lesions are identified in the imaged osseus structures.


PROCEDURAL NOTE FOR RIGHT HEPATIC LOBE RADIOFREQUENCY ABLATION:

PROCEDURE:
1.  Ultrasound-guided RF ablation of presumed HCC spanning segments V and VI.
2.  Ultrasound evaluation of the left hepatic lobe lesion in the junction of
left hepatic segments II and III.
3.  18-gauge core biopsy of the right hepatic lobe lesions.
4.  Gelfoam embolization of the biopsy tract. 

HISTORY:  ___ male with cirrhosis and two hyperenhancing lesions in
the right and left hepatic lobes respectively.  Request is to perform RFA of
one or both lesions if feasible.

PROCEDURE:  General anesthesia was provided by the anesthesiology service. 
Please see relevant documentation.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the procedure. 
Dr. ___ attending radiologist, was present throughout the procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Informed consent was obtained in the outpatient
clinic outlining the risks and benefits of the procedure involved.  Following
this, the patient was brought to the CT suite and placed supine on the imaging
table.  Following induction of general anesthesia, the abdomen was prepped and
draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure huddle and timeout were
performed as per ___ protocol.

Initially, the right hepatic lobe was targeted.  Ultrasound demonstrated a
hyperechoic mass lesion in the expected position.  Under real-time ultrasound
guidance, a 17-gauge biopsy needle was advanced and positioned within the
proximal portion of the lesion.  Two 18-gauge core biopsies were then taken. 
Samples were placed in formalin and sent for pathological assessment.  The
biopsy tract was then embolized with a Gelfoam slurry and good hemostasis was
achieved.  Following biopsy, an 18 gauge RF ablation probe was positioned
within the inferior segment of the right hepatic lobe lesion.  Following a
safety check confirming adequate positioning of the grounding pads an ablation
was performed of the lesion.  Gas formation was noted on real-time ultrasound.
The needle was then repositioned slightly more cranially to ensure a
satisfactory ablation zone and ablation again performed.
Following this, the needle was removed.  A contrast-enhanced CT was performed
(see report above).  Ultrasound was then used to try to target the left
hepatic lobe lesion.  This lesion was not visible on ultrasound and given its
proximity on the CT to adjacent colon and stomach, a decision was made not to
proceed with RF ablation at this time.  
Sterile dressings were applied.  
The patient was transferred well to the post-anesthesia care unit.

IMPRESSION:

1. Satisfactory 18G core biopsy (two cores taken) of the  right hepatic lobe
lesion with successful radiofrequency ablation.  
2. Ultrasound evaluation of the left hepatic lobe lesion demonstrated the
lesion not to be amenable to percutaneous RFA.  
3. A contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated satisfactory ablation zone surrounding
the right hepatic tumor with close proximity of the left hepatic lobe lesion
to stomach and colon.

The staff radiologist has reviewed the images and the report.

EXAMINATION: 
Targeted liver ultrasound to target right hepatic lobe hyperechoic lesion for
radiofrequency ablation.

INDICATION:
___ male with cirrhosis and hyperechoic lesion in right hepatic lobe
consistent for hepatocellular carcinoma.

Ultrasound was used to perform an 18-gauge core biopsy and to position a RF
probe within the right hepatic lesion.  
Please see full report of the procedure under CT, using clip ___.  

IMPRESSION:  Ultrasound images demonstrate satisfactory biopsy needle and RF
tip position for right hepatic lobe radiofrequency ablation.

The staff radiologist has reviewed the images and the report.

AP CHEST 12:28 P.M., ___.  

HISTORY:  Hepatitis C.  Alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma.  Fever
after radiofrequency ablation.  Possible pneumonia.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Moderate cardiomegaly has increased.  Left lung is clear.  At the base of the
right lung is a moderate pleural effusion which obscures the features of the
right lower lobe.

INDICATION:  ___ male with alcohol and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis.
The patient is ___ hours post-radiofrequency ablation of a segment VI
hepatocellular carcinoma.  The patient has had a 10-point hematocrit drop and
episode of orthostatic hypotension. 
Request is to evaluate for possible occult hemorrhage.

COMPARISON:  Reference is made to the CT acquisitions from the RF ablation
dated ___ and also from the pre-procedural MR abdomen with contrast
dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT was used to acquire non-contrast, arterial,
portal venous and delayed phase imaging of the liver and upper abdomen.  In
addition, a non-contrast CT thorax was performed.  Coronal and sagittal
reformats were evaluated.

NON-CONTRAST CT OF THORAX:  There has been interval development of a large
right-sided pleural effusion.  The ___ unit density of the fusion is
between 40 and 50 indicative of hyperdense proteinaceous fluid, likely blood.
There is associated extensive right lower lobe collapse. No evidence of a
layering hematocrit level.  There is no pneumothorax.  Patchy air space
opacity is noted in the apical segment of the left upper lobe, likely
inflammatory in etiology. 


CT OF ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST: 

There has been a decrease in the amount of perihepatic and perisplenic fluid
since the RF procedure.  There is satisfactory appearance of the ablated
lesion in segment VI of the liver.  There is no evidence of active arterial
extravasation on the arterial phase images.  Note is made, however, of
segmental arterial portal venous shunting just medial to the ablated segment.
The ablation zone measures 2 x 3.8 x 2.9 cm.  A second hyperenhancing lesion
is again identified arising exophytically from segment III of the liver.
No other arterial enhancing lesions are identified.

Changes of cirrhosis and portal hypertension are again noted.  The liver has a
coarse and irregular outline. The spleen is enlarged measuring 14 cm in
craniocaudal dimension.  There are paraesophageal and splenic hilar varices.
Note is also made of a left-sided splenorenal shunt.  
Note is also made of a markedly enlarged and recanalized umbilical vein. There
is no significant bowel wall thickening.  Both kidneys enhance symmetrically.
Normal appearance of both adrenal glands.    Although incompletely imaged, the
most inferior slice demonstrates a patent vessel in the anterior abdominal
wall likely secondary to paraumbilical varices (series 3BH, image 186).
A large gallstone is again identified.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  Mild endplate degenerative changes are seen throughout
the lower thoracic and upper lumbar vertebrae.  No evidence of a lytic or
sclerotic lesion .

IMPRESSION:  
1. Interval development of a large right-sided hemothorax with resulting
collapse of the right lower lobe.  
2. Expected appearance of the segment VI ablation zone.  
3. No evidence of active arterial hemorrhage.  
4. Unchanged appearance of the hyperenhancing exophytic lesion arising from
segment III of the left lobe of liver.

AP CHEST, 9:41 A.M., ___

INDICATION:  A ___ man with HCV cirrhosis resolving hemothorax. 
Question pulmonary edema or effusion.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

ONE VIEW OF THE CHEST:

The lungs are low in volume and show improvement in bilateral focal airspace
opacities.  A mild right lower lobe opacity could represent atelectasis.  The
cardiac silhouette is enlarged, unchanged.  The mediastinal silhouette and
hilar contours are normal.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is present. 
Subcutaneous gas is noted along the right chest wall.

IMPRESSION:

Interval improvement in pulmonary edema.  Right lower lobe opacity could
represent pneumonia or atelectasis. 

Note that radiography cannot detect fluid collections in the soft tissues, a
CT scan is recommended if that continues to be a clinical concern.  If a CT
scan is not obtained, a dedicated PA and lateral radiograph can help in better
evaluation of the right lower lobe opacity.
